formation.title: Suvarnabhumi: The Land of Gold
formation.text:
What the Pali sutras called Suvarnabhumi (the Golden Land) has come at last under one banner. The wat-temples of Angkor and the chedis of Ayutthaya, the stupa-strewn plain of Bagan and the That Luang of Vientiane, all four civilizational anchors of mainland Southeast Asia answer to a single Buddhist universal monarch. Bayinnaung held this scope briefly before fragmentation; the Khmer Empire dreamed of it before Thai expansion eroded its frontiers; King Lithai imagined it as the mortal-realm Mount Meru of the Trai Phum cosmology. Now the saffron-and-gold dharma-wheel banner flies over every mainland kingdom from Pagan to the Mekong delta. But what is Suvarnabhumi to be: a single sacral throne, a federation under one sangha, or the Three Worlds made flesh?

This choice unlocks a destiny path in the Traditions tab.

options.text: Cakkavatti: the universal monarch turns the wheel

modifiers.name: Cakkavatti: The Wheel-Turning Monarch
modifiers.text: The king is bodhisattva and dhamma-raja, the universal monarch who turns the wheel of the law. Centralized sacral kingship in the manner of Angkor's Jayavarman VII and Toungoo Bayinnaung: armies advance under the saffron banner, and the prestige of the throne radiates outward across the mandala.

options.text: Sangha Federation: kings divided, dharma united

modifiers.name: The Sangha Federation
modifiers.text: What binds Suvarnabhumi is not the throne but the trans-mainland Buddhist monastic order. Each Khmer, Thai, Burmese, Mon, and Lao king governs his own people, but every saffron-robed monk crosses every border, and the sangha is the empire. Loose suzerainty, broad tolerance, and the dharma as the only universal law.

options.text: The Three Worlds: empire as cosmic order

modifiers.name: The Three Worlds Empire
modifiers.text: King Lithai's Trai Phum Phra Ruang made the empire a mortal-realm reflection of the Buddhist cosmos. Court ceremony, sumptuary law, and karmic-merit hierarchy are all theatrical performances of cosmological order: the king as Mount Meru at the center, the realms of gods, men, and hells radiating outward in elaborate ritual pageantry.

advances.name: Baray Engineering
advances.text: The Khmer hydraulic-city tradition of monsoon water management: vast reservoirs, canal networks, and embankments that captured the wet season's floods to recharge the dry season's paddy fields.

event.title: The Hydraulic City
event.text: Across one thousand square kilometers of the Angkor plain, our engineers have completed the network of barays, canals, moats, and embankments that gave the Khmer Empire its agricultural foundation. The West Baray alone holds enough water to recharge the dry-season groundwater table for the whole region; the Jayatataka supplies the city itself. Twin monsoon floods are tamed, paddy is double-cropped, and what was sustained engineering brilliance under Suryavarman now serves a renewed Suvarnabhumi. The fourteenth-century droughts that broke Angkor's old hydraulic city will not break ours. We have learned from history.

options.text: The Land of Gold drinks deep

advances.name: The Pali Sangha
advances.text: Adopting Pali as the canonical liturgical language unites the trans-mainland Theravada monastic order: Khmer, Mon, Burmese, Thai, and Lao monks all chant the same suttas, cross every border, and form a continuous spiritual fabric.

advances.name: Wat-Temple Architecture
advances.text: The Indianized stone-temple tradition that produced Angkor Wat, the Bayon, and Bagan's stupa-strewn plain: sandstone and laterite assembled into mountain-temple complexes that anchor the spiritual geography of the realm.

advances.name: Riverine Warfare
advances.text: Long teak war canoes manned by drummed-rowed crews, fighting on the Mekong, the Chao Phraya, and the Irrawaddy. These are the great river systems that are mainland Southeast Asia's true highways.

advances.name: Monsoon Paddy Intensification
advances.text: Wet-rice double-cropping along the great rivers, sustained by communal labor mobilization and traditional water management: the agricultural foundation that allowed Angkor and Pagan to feed their imperial populations.

advances.name: Bronze Buddha Foundry
advances.text: The lost-wax casting of bronze Buddha images, a major artistic-religious industry from the Sukhothai walking Buddhas to the seated Mara-victories of Mandalay. State foundries supply the temples; donor patronage funds the casting; merit accrues to king and devotee alike.

advances.name: Royal Chedi-Stupa Construction
advances.text: Monumental relic-mound construction as legitimacy theater: every king must crown a chedi, and the great gilded spires of Pegu, Ayutthaya, and Vientiane mark the dynastic genealogy of the empire.

advances.name: Sinhalese Ordination Reform
advances.text: Importing senior monks from Sri Lanka to re-ordain the local sangha and establish a 'pure' Mahavihara lineage: the reform pattern that ran from Anawrahta's Bagan and Ramkhamhaeng's Sukhothai down to the eighteenth-century reordinations of mainland Theravada.

event.title: The Sinhalese Ordination
event.text: Senior monks have arrived from Sri Lanka, heirs of the Mahavihara orthodoxy, bearing the full Pali canon and the unbroken Theravada lineage stretching back to the Third Buddhist Council. As King Anawrahta did at Bagan, as Ramkhamhaeng did at Sukhothai, we now invite them to re-ordain our own sangha and establish a 'pure' Sinhala lineage. The reformed sangha will bind every monastery from the Irrawaddy to the Mekong under one ordination. But who shall command it: the throne, or the forest hermitage?

options.text: The sangha-raja answers to the throne

modifiers.name: State-Aligned Sangha
modifiers.text: The reformed sangha-raja hierarchy reports directly to the throne. Royal ordination councils enforce orthodoxy and ritual purity throughout the empire.

options.text: Honor the forest-dwelling masters

modifiers.name: Forest Sangha Tradition
modifiers.text: The forest-dwelling meditation monks remain the spiritual elite, drawing lay devotion across cultural lines and fostering popular Buddhist piety.

advances.name: Royal Elephant Kraal Doctrine
advances.text: The mass capture and training of war elephants. Khmer, Thai, and Burmese kings all maintained royal kraals where wild herds were corralled, broken to harness, and trained for battle, parade, and royal hunts. The institutional doctrine that produced the empire's elephant corps.

advances.name: Mandala Statecraft
advances.text: The Indianized concentric-tributary kingship model: a divine-king at the cosmic center surrounded by sub-kings owing personal allegiance, a system that scales from a single river-valley capital to a pan-mainland empire.

advances.name: Toungoo Elephant Doctrine
advances.text: Bayinnaung's signature: massed columns of war elephants in disciplined heavy-shock formations, supported by infantry and cavalry. The Portuguese described his elephant corps as the most formidable in Asia, eclipsing even the Mughal mass.

advances.name: The Great River Ports
advances.text: Establishing entrepot ports at the mouths and confluences of the Mekong, the Chao Phraya, and the Irrawaddy. These river-mouth trading cities bind upcountry rice and gemstones to the maritime spice routes.

advances.name: Gemstone Trade Monopolies
advances.text: Burmese rubies from the Mogok valley, Cambodian sapphires from Pailin, and the spinels and pearls of the inland trade: royal monopolies on the mainland's gem fields, sold through Ayutthaya and Pegu to the world.

advances.name: Bayinnaung Doctrine
advances.text: The strategic blueprint of pan-mainland conquest: rapid mobilization of multi-cultural levies, mass-elephant assault columns, and the suppression of Shan rebels and Lao resistance through overwhelming concentration of force.

event.title: Bayinnaung's Vision Fulfilled
event.text: By 1580, the Toungoo king Bayinnaung (what the Portuguese called the most powerful monarch in Asia after the emperor of China) had assembled the largest contiguous polity in Southeast Asian history: Burma proper, the Shan States, Lan Na, Lan Xang, Manipur, and Ayutthaya itself, all sworn vassals to Pegu. He held it together by personal allegiance to the Cakkavatti, ruling from a single capital with no institutional successor. Within a generation of his death, the empire fragmented. We have done what he could not: the doctrine of pan-mainland conquest fulfilled. But how shall we hold what he lost?

options.text: Make every conqueror a Suvarnabhumin

modifiers.name: Indochinese Synthesis
modifiers.text: The conquered Mon, Khmer, and Lao are not subjects but Suvarnabhumin in the making: Theravada Buddhism is the universal solvent.

options.text: Rule through the mandala of sub-kings

modifiers.name: Mandala of Tributaries
modifiers.text: Bayinnaung's model: sub-kings retain their thrones and provide elephant-corps levies in turn for tribute, prestige, and protection.

advances.name: Lacquerware Tradition
advances.text: The Burmese yun and Thai lai-rod-nam court crafts: sap-of-the-thitsi-tree lacquer applied in many layers to bamboo and wood, then incised, gilded, or inlaid with mother-of-pearl. A signature export of the mainland courts.

advances.name: The Cakkavatti Royal Guard
advances.text: The elite household infantry of the universal monarch: palace guards drawn from soldier-castes, drilled in the king's own compound, and answerable directly to the throne. The personal retinue of the dhamma-raja.

advances.name: Cosmopolitan Court
advances.text: The capital becomes the diplomatic crossroads of Eurasia: Persian Shi'ite ministers, Japanese mercenary captains, French Jesuit emissaries, Dutch VOC factors, and Chinese tea-merchants all enrolled at court, each in their own assigned quarter.

event.title: The Cosmopolitan Court
event.text: Embassies arrive: French Jesuits, Persian Shi'ites with the merchant lord Sheikh Ahmad, Japanese ronin retainers, Dutch VOC factors, Chinese tea-traders, English East India Company envoys, and Indian Muslim port-officials all jostling for position at the capital. Persian quarters and Japanese settlements line the riverfront alongside Portuguese churches and Chinese pagodas. The empire has become, as Ayutthaya was under Narai, a turntable of Eurasian commerce. Shall we throw the gates wide, or carefully select our partners?

options.text: All quarters, all flags welcome

modifiers.name: The Cosmopolitan Court
modifiers.text: Like King Narai's Ayutthaya, the capital hosts Persian, Japanese, French, Dutch, Chinese, and Indian quarters. The empire becomes a turntable of Eurasian commerce.

options.text: Elevate chosen foreigners; control the rest

modifiers.name: Chosen Foreign Advisors
modifiers.text: Like Sheikh Ahmad and Constantine Phaulkon, select foreigners are elevated to high office while the kingdom's commerce remains under royal monopoly.

advances.name: Trai Phum Cosmology
advances.text: King Lithai's Three Worlds According to King Ruang, the canonical Buddhist cosmology of mainland Southeast Asian statecraft, mapping thirty-one realms from the Avici hells through human existence to the formless heavens of the Brahmas.

event.title: The Three Worlds Codified
event.text: King Lithai's Trai Phum Phra Ruang (the Three Worlds According to King Ruang) has become the canonical ideology of statecraft. Composed in 1345 as the oldest known work of Thai literature, it maps the thirty-one realms of Buddhist cosmology: eleven levels of the desire-realm Kamadhatu, sixteen of the form-realm Rupadhatu, four of the formless Arupadhatu. Every painted hell-scene at every wat now reminds the laity that good karma leads to heaven and evil to torment. The empire is reframed as the mortal mirror of Mount Meru, and the king reigns at the cosmic center.

options.text: Let every wat paint the realms anew

advances.name: Royal Sumptuary Law
advances.text: Elaborate gradation of dress, parasol-tiers, palanquin-types, and ceremonial speech-registers, all encoding karmic-merit hierarchy in visible form. The court becomes a living theatre of cosmological order.

advances.name: Early Matchlock Adoption
advances.text: Portuguese mercenaries and traders bring matchlock muskets and bronze cannons to mainland courts. Diogo Soares de Mello served at Ayutthaya, Filipe de Brito ruled Syriam: the Iberian gunpowder revolution arrives early on the Bay of Bengal.

advances.name: Reformist Sangha
advances.text: Reformist saffron-robed monastics actively shape state policy, mediate disputes, and lead lay piety movements. The sangha-state alliance becomes the empire's spiritual bone.

advances.name: Burmese Musketeer Corps
advances.text: Standing matchlock infantry recruited from the rural hinterland and drilled at royal cantonments, Konbaung's signature force, deployed in disciplined volleys and trained in jungle and wetland combat.

advances.name: Konbaung Military Reform
advances.text: Alaungpaya's organizational reforms: standardized levy recruitment from rural districts, integrated firearms training, and royal decrees on musket handling, transforming traditional mass-elephant levies into a hybrid gunpowder army.

event.title: Konbaung's Gunpowder Reform
event.text: Alaungpaya, founder of the Konbaung line, has decreed standardized matchlock training and disciplined volley-fire formations. Teak war-boats now carry up to thirty musketeers and 6-pounder swivel cannon; siege artillery is mounted on wooden platforms to clear walls. French gunners, drifted east after Pondicherry's troubles, drill our infantry in European fashion. Shall we follow their model wholesale, or build our own arsenal?

options.text: Adopt the European drill manual

modifiers.name: French Drill Manual
modifiers.text: Konbaung infantry drill on the European model: disciplined matchlock formations, volley fire, and bayonet-equipped musketeers serving as elite corps.

options.text: Royal arsenals, Burmese pattern

modifiers.name: The Burmese Royal Arsenal
modifiers.text: State-run gun foundries cast firearms locally rather than importing them, supplying the rapidly expanding levies of the late empire.

advances.name: Theravada State Religion
advances.text: The formal codification of Theravada Buddhism as imperial state ideology: royal dhamma-raja titulature, state ordination councils, and chedi-construction tied to dynastic legitimacy.

advances.name: Imperial Pilgrim Roads
advances.text: The great trunk roads connecting the wat-temple sites of the empire: pilgrim routes that double as troop-march and tax-collector roads, knitting the river-valley capitals into a single administrative fabric.

advances.name: Protector of the Dharma
advances.text: The royal title sasana-bhirakkhita, protector of the Buddhist dispensation. The king maintains the sangha, sponsors the canonical councils, and gilds the great chedis as karmic merit accruing to throne and dynasty.

advances.name: Konbaung Jingal Artillery
advances.text: Pivot-mounted swivel guns and zumbooruks: large-bore wall pieces and camel-mounted small cannon that bridged the gap between musket and field artillery in the late Burmese armies.

advances.name: Pan-Mainland Identity
advances.text: The shared Theravada civilizational consciousness becomes a self-aware imperial identity: Suvarnabhumin, not Khmer or Thai or Burmese, is what the educated subject increasingly calls themselves.

advances.name: Resist Colonial Penetration
advances.text: Where the historical fragmented mainland fell piecewise to British Burma, French Indochina, and the unequal treaties imposed on Siam, a unified Suvarnabhumi confronts European expansion as a single great power, and may yet hold the line.

advances.name: Industrial Rice Export
advances.text: The Chao Phraya and Irrawaddy deltas, drained and double-cropped on an industrial scale, become the rice basket of monsoon Asia, feeding Singapore, Hong Kong, Calcutta, and the labor lines of the South China Sea.

destiny.name: Suvarnabhumi Destined
destiny.text: The Land of Gold awakens to its imperial vocation. From the wat-spires of Pagan to the chedis of Vientiane, the Cakkavatti's wheel begins to turn. Achieve stability 25 to consolidate the new order and unlock a destiny path.

conditions.text: Stability at least 25

event.title: The Wheel Turns
event.text: What was prophesied in the Sutta Pitaka has come at last: a Cakkavatti has arisen in the Land of Gold, and the wheel of the dharma turns again. From the western Irrawaddy to the eastern Mekong, monasteries fly the saffron banner; from the Cham coast to the Sri Lankan straits, embassies seek out the universal monarch. The court astrologers cast horoscopes; the ministers debate doctrine. The road ahead branches: shall the Wheel be turned by the sword of conquest, or by the gentler turning of the dharma's law?

options.text: Let the wheel turn.

destiny.name: The Champa Conquest
destiny.text: The Cham coastal cities (Simhapura, Vijaya, Panduranga) must fall to the saffron banner before the eastern frontier can be secured. Push elephant columns across the Annamite range and break the last Hindu kingdom of mainland Southeast Asia. Required: own Simhapura, Vijaya and Panduranga.

conditions.text: Path: Cakkavatti, Universal Buddhist Monarch.
Own Simhapura, or a subject owns it
Own Vijaya, or a subject owns it
Own Panduranga, or a subject owns it

event.title: The Cham Coast Falls
event.text: Simhapura's red-brick towers, Vijaya's harbor walls: the last Cham strongholds have surrendered to our elephant corps. The Hindu kingdom that fought Khmer and Đại Việt for a thousand years bows at last to a Buddhist universal monarch. The eastern frontier is secured; the South China Sea opens to our shipping. The Annamite range, that ancient barrier between mainland and coast, is no longer a frontier but an inner road.

options.text: Onward to the Red River.

destiny.name: The Red River Submits
destiny.text: Đại Việt held the Red River against southern empires for a millennium. To complete the Cakkavatti's circuit, even Thăng Long must answer to the throne of the wheel. Required: own Thăng Long, hold half of the Red River delta, keep Elephant Kraals or Elephant Hunting Grounds in four locations.

conditions.text: Own Thăng Long, or a subject owns it
At least 50% of the locations of the Red River Delta are ours
At least 4 of our locations have an Elephant Kraal or Elephant Hunting Grounds

event.title: Thăng Long Submits
event.text: Where Lê dynasty Đại Việt repulsed Mongol khans and Ming emperors, our forces have done what no southern power achieved: taken Thăng Long itself. The Red River delta, with its dense rice-population and fortified citadels, now answers to the Cakkavatti. The question is how to govern this most ancient and most stubborn of mainland kingdoms: as Suvarnabhumin like all the rest, or as a perpetually garrisoned northern march?

options.text: Make Đại Việt a Suvarnabhumi province.

modifiers.name: Đại Việt Subjugated
modifiers.text: The Red River delta is folded into Suvarnabhumi proper. Veteran armies push outward, casus belli are easy to come by, and the long supply lines of empire extend beyond the monsoon rains.

options.text: Garrison the Red River as a northern march.

modifiers.name: The Red River Garrison
modifiers.text: The Đại Việt frontier is held as a fortified northern march: heavy garrisons, long defensive walls along the Hồng River, and locally-recruited levy regiments that can be mobilized in season.

destiny.name: Universal Monarch's Realm
destiny.text: Yunnan in the north, Malacca and Temasek in the south: the four cardinal anchors of the Cakkavatti's wheel, and a ring of subject kings around its hub. What Bayinnaung lost in a generation, we hold by destiny. Unlocks the Cakkavatti's Throne. Required: own Kunming, Malacca, and Temasek, four subjects, prestige 75.

conditions.text: Own Kūnmíng, or a subject owns it
Own Malacca, or a subject owns it
Own Temasek, or a subject owns it
Num subjects at least 4
Prestige at least 75

event.title: The Universal Monarch's Realm
event.text: Kunming in the north, Malacca and Temasek in the south: the four cardinal anchors are ours. From the Tai-Yi salt-mines of Yunnan to the spice quays of the Strait, from the Cham coast to the Sinhalese ordination-axis, the entire mandala of mainland Southeast Asia answers to one Cakkavatti. The dhamma-raja sits at the cosmic center, and the saffron wheel turns over a domain Bayinnaung could only dream of holding. Now we must decide what kind of empire this is to be: a centralized dharma-imperium administered from a single throne, or the apex of a tributary mandala in which sub-kings rule under the universal monarch's protection?

options.text: A unified dharma-imperium.

modifiers.name: The Dharma Imperium
modifiers.text: A single sacral throne rules the mainland from Pagan to Tonkin. Conquered cultures integrate quickly, the rice-baskets of the great deltas feed the imperial population, and the levy-ban resources can be mobilized at speed.

options.text: The mandala of sub-kings reaches its apex.

modifiers.name: The Mandala at Apex
modifiers.text: The tributary system reaches its peak: sub-kings at Pegu, Ayutthaya, Lan Xang, and Đại Việt provide elephant-corps levies and rapid-march support, but the sangha must feed itself across vast distances.

destiny.name: The Sinhalese Axis
destiny.text: The trans-mainland sangha is born from the Mahavihara at Anuradhapura. Re-establish the Sinhalese ordination axis with mainland endowments and one written monastic law to bind every monastery in one orthodoxy. Required: own Anuradhapura, gold 1000, a Pali Monastic College in two towns.

conditions.text: Path: Sangha Federation, kings divided, dharma united.
Own Anuradhapura, or a subject owns it
Gold at least 1000
A Pali Monastic College stands in at least 2 of our locations

event.title: The Mahavihara Lineage
event.text: Senior monks have arrived from the Mahavihara at Anuradhapura, bearing the unbroken Sinhalese ordination back to its mainland disciples. Where Anawrahta and Ramkhamhaeng received it piecemeal, we hold the entire axis: Anuradhapura, Pagan, Ayutthaya, Vientiane, the scriptoria already at work copying the Tipitaka in Pali, Khmer, Burmese, Mon, and Lao scripts. The sangha is now a single fabric stretching from the Sri Lankan dagobas to the Mekong delta.

options.text: The orthodoxy is established.

destiny.name: Three Worlds Made Flesh
destiny.text: Trai Phum cosmology demands that the empire be a mortal-realm mirror of Mount Meru: gilded chedis, lacquered halls, gem-encrusted Buddha images. The luxury-export economy underwrites the cosmological state. Sukhothai, where the Trai Phum was written, is to be built up as its seat. Required: own Sukhothai with development 42, gems and lacquerware in your markets, prestige 50.

conditions.text: Sukhothai is ours and its development is at least 42
A market the country is in

children.text: Gems is produced in the market
Gems is traded in the market

conditions.text: A market the country is in

children.text: Lacquerware is produced in the market
Lacquerware is traded in the market

conditions.text: Prestige at least 50

event.title: The Three Worlds Codified
event.text: King Lithai's Trai Phum has become the imperial cosmology: every wat hall painted with the thirty-one realms, every chedi gilded as a mortal Mount Meru, every Buddha image cast in bronze and lacquer-finished by court ateliers. Mogok rubies, Pailin sapphires, and the goldsmith's craft of Ayutthaya supply the empire's visible wealth. The civilizational ideology demands an organizational core to sustain it: shall the court ateliers concentrate craftsmanship at the capital, or shall the merit-economy of pilgrimage routes spread prosperity across the wat-temples of the realm?

options.text: Concentrate craft at the court.

modifiers.name: Court Atelier System
modifiers.text: The royal workshops of Pegu, Ayutthaya, and Vientiane concentrate the empire's master artisans: gilded glassware, gem-set lacquer, and the burgher guilds prosper under royal protection.

options.text: Cultivate the pilgrim economy of the wats.

modifiers.name: The Pilgrim Economy
modifiers.text: The great wat-temple network draws lay devotion across the empire: pilgrim quarters fill the towns, monastic dispensaries spread medical knowledge, and the merit-economy lubricates ordinary commerce.

effects.name: Possible Burghers in Towns and Cities
Possible Clerics in Towns and Cities

destiny.name: The Civilization of Suvarnabhumi
destiny.text: From Pagan's manuscript libraries to Ayutthaya's Persian quarters, the empire becomes the Eurasian crossroads of letters and learning. A unified Theravada civilization, prosperous and literate, takes its place among the great empires of the world. Unlocks the Pali University. Required: average literacy of 30, a library in Pagan, gold 3000, own Pagan with development 59.

conditions.text: Average country literacy at least 30
Our Pagan has a Library
Gold at least 3000
Pagan is ours and its development is at least 59

event.title: The Civilization of Suvarnabhumi
event.text: From Pagan's palm-leaf libraries to Ayutthaya's Persian quarter, from the Mahavihara monks to the Konbaung astronomers, Suvarnabhumi has become a self-aware civilization, peer of the Ming court, the Mughal durbar, the Ottoman Porte, and the European chancelleries. Pali commentaries, court chronicles, and astronomical treatises pour from the printing presses. The sangha-state has produced its own renaissance. Now the elders debate the empire's intellectual settlement: a flourishing of textual scholarship across all schools, or a single canonical council to fix the orthodoxy for ages to come?

options.text: A flourishing of Pali letters.

modifiers.name: The Pali Renaissance
modifiers.text: Printing presses pour out Pali commentaries, Khmer chronicles, and Burmese astronomical treatises. Literacy spreads from the monasteries to the lay population, and the empire heals quickly from the wars of conquest.

options.text: Convene the canonical council.

modifiers.name: The Canonical Council
modifiers.text: A single great council fixes the orthodox Tipitaka for all of Suvarnabhumi. Clergy power and noble literacy rise together, but heterodox schools are suppressed and the political settlement is uneasy.

units.name: War Canoe
units.text: Long teak fighting canoe rowed by drummed crews, mounting bow chasers and packed with javelin-and-firearm marines. Fast and thin-hulled. The signature riverine warship of mainland Southeast Asia.

units.name: Toungoo War Elephant
units.text: Mass-elephant heavy shock cavalry in the Toungoo manner: armored war elephants in massed columns, each carrying mahout, archers, and matchlock men in the howdah, deployed in disciplined assault lines.

units.name: Cakkavatti Royal Guard
units.text: Elite household heavy infantry of the dhamma-raja: armored palace guards drawn from soldier-caste families, sworn personally to the universal monarch.

units.name: Cakkavatti Royal Guard
units.text: Levy form of the Cakkavatti Royal Guard.

units.name: Burmese Musketeer
units.text: Konbaung-era matchlock light infantry, trained in jungle and wetland combat. The mainstay of the late mainland gunpowder army, equally at home in stockade defense and amphibious assault.

units.name: Burmese Musketeer
units.text: Levy form of the Burmese Musketeer.

units.name: Jingal Artillery
units.text: Konbaung swivel-gun and camel-borne zumbooruk crews: the late Burmese answer to European field artillery, mobile and well-suited to the river-valley terrain of the empire.

buildings.name: Royal Baray
buildings.text: The vast earthen-embankment monsoon reservoir of the Khmer hydraulic city: capturing wet-season floods to feed dry-season paddy and recharging the regional water table for sustained agricultural intensification.

where.text: The location's raw material is Rice

buildings.name: Pali Monastic College
buildings.text: A residential teaching monastery where Pali grammar, the Tipitaka canon, and Abhidhamma philosophy are taught to ordained monks, the spiritual and educational backbone of the trans-mainland sangha.

buildings.name: Royal Wat-Temple
buildings.text: An Angkor or Bagan style stone-temple complex: concentric galleries, central prang or stupa-spire, libraries, ordination hall, and surrounding monk-quarters. The spiritual anchor of the surrounding region.

buildings.name: Bronze Buddha Foundry
buildings.text: The lost-wax casting workshop where bronze Buddha images, ceremonial bells, and gilded ritual vessels are produced for temples across the empire and for export, a major consumer-goods industry tied to religious devotion.

buildings.name: Royal Chedi-Stupa
buildings.text: A monumental gilded relic-mound: the dynastic merit-monument of mainland Theravada kingship, marking the central axis of the capital and gathering pilgrim devotion across the realm.

effect_groups.label: To the country, when built in the capital

buildings.name: Royal Elephant Kraal
buildings.text: A massive timber-stockade compound where wild elephants are corralled, sorted, broken to harness, and trained, the breeding and training ground of the empire's war-elephant corps.

where.text: The location's raw material is Elephants

buildings.name: Riverine Entrepot Port
buildings.text: A walled river-mouth port, such as Bago, Ayutthaya, Phnom Penh, Vientiane, or Yangon: fortified warehouses, foreign quarters, and stone docks that anchor the empire's river-based commerce to the maritime spice routes.

buildings.name: Lacquerware Atelier
buildings.text: A guild workshop producing Burmese yun and Thai lai-rod-nam lacquerware: sap-of-the-thitsi-tree applied in many layers to bamboo and wood, then incised, gilded, or inlaid with mother-of-pearl. The signature luxury export of the mainland courts.

buildings.name: Royal Gem Workshop
buildings.text: A guild atelier where Mogok rubies, Pailin sapphires, and the spinels and pearls of the inland trade are cut, polished, and set in gold for the royal court and the export market.

buildings.name: Royal Arsenal
buildings.text: A state-run gun foundry and powder mill: saltpeter from inland deposits, iron from the hills, copper and the tin of the Tenasserim coast for the bronze, and lumber from the teak forests are made into matchlock muskets, swivel guns, and bronze cannons under royal monopoly.

buildings.name: Cakkavatti's Throne
buildings.text: The universal monarch's audience hall: a vast pillared chamber at the cosmic center of the realm, where ambassadors from the four cardinal directions kneel before the dhamma-raja. Capital only.

effect_groups.label: To the country, when built in the capital

buildings.name: Pali University
buildings.text: A great trans-mainland scholastic monastery: printing presses turning out the Tipitaka, lecture halls debating Abhidhamma philosophy, and Pali grammar taught alongside Sanskrit, Persian, and astronomical sciences. The intellectual capital of Theravada civilization.

list.name: Royal Sangha Council
list.text: A state-appointed Sangharaja and a council of elder theras (the Sudhamma model formalized by Bayinnaung's 1560s sasana-purification reforms and the Burmese Thathanabaing of 1784) certify ordinations, police monastic discipline, and arbitrate doctrinal disputes across the trans-mainland sangha. Theravada cohesion becomes a binding institution above any one realm, but provincial abbots resent central oversight.

list.name: Sakdina Hierarchy
list.text: King Borommatrailokkanat's 1454 codification of dignity-rank: every subject is assigned a numerical sakdina corresponding to rai of land, governing court precedence, service-grant entitlement, and even legal procedure (testimony weight scaled to rank). The defining administrative innovation of Ayutthaya, copied across the Tai-Khmer-Mon world.

list.name: Mandala Tributary Ring
list.text: The Indianized circle-of-kings: a paramount cakkavatti at the cosmic center, ringed by tributary kings paying bunga mas, kneeling at coronation, and providing levies in war. Bayinnaung's 1564 reduction of Maha Chakkraphat to vassal-king of Pegu is the textbook case. Sovereignty radiates from prestige, not from fixed borders.

list.name: Court Brahmin College
list.text: The Phra Maha Rajaguru and the Devasathan: court Brahmins retained from pre-Theravada Indianization to perform coronation rites (Borommatrailokkanat's 1460s ceremony), the Trīyampawāi seasonal swing-rituals, and astrological-cosmological consultation. A foreign-stock specialist caste serving the throne directly, sidestepping both the sangha and the noble hierarchy.

list.name: Royal Elephant Corps
list.text: The king's elephant stable: war-elephant breeding, a hereditary mahout caste, and the cosmological 'elephant treasure' that marks the seven regalia of a universal monarch. Bayinnaung's 1563 white-elephant war against Ayutthaya turned a captured albino into a casus belli. The corps is at once military shock, royal prestige, and Buddhist iconography.

list.name: Phrai Corvée Registry
list.text: The Ayutthaya labor draft. Free commoners (phrai luang) are registered to nai master-officials and owe six months of royal service per year: public works, monsoon dyke repair, royal granary, military mobilization. Codified alongside sakdina but mechanically distinct: this is the mobilization base of the realm. Nobles fight over phrai-counts more bitterly than over land.
